chapter_title: Concerning the Seven Works of the Living Spirit

3.original: [The second: He spread about the one who had rebelled, he crucified ]
3.content: The second: He spread about the one who had rebelled, he crucified

spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation: The Seven Works of the Divine Operative Power

---

**¶1:** The Lord's divine operative power has accomplished seven complete acts of regeneration through its omnipotence.

**¶2:** The first: It raised the celestial state of the human will out of the combat of spiritual temptation, in the manner that a precious interior truth is [GAP-1] drawn up from the abyss of the natural mind overwhelmed by falsities.

**¶3:** [GAP-2: The second: It laid open the selfhood that had risen in rebellion, and fixed] it fast within every external form — so that the evil of self-love could no longer act freely in any natural degree.

**¶4:** The third: It subjugated, confined, and penetrated the inmost qualities of spiritual death — that is, evil and falsity in their very essences — so that they were utterly overthrown.

**¶5:** The fourth: It fashioned the vessels capable of receiving and carrying divine wisdom — containing forms structured to bear the light of truth through all degrees.

**¶6:** The fifth: It called forth its five interior faculties of spiritual perception and arranged them in their order. They [GAP-3] assumed governance of the ordered spiritual sphere, and they sustained the burden of every state in the whole of existence. It also called forth three essential divine truths, alive with the Lord's life. It set [GAP-4] each upon one of the three containing forms corresponding to the three degrees of the mind — celestial, spiritual, and natural — and another upon the gross external natural man. [GAP-5] It further called forth the divine invitation — the influx of the Lord's calling — so that it might be conjoined with the five illuminated perceptive faculties.

**¶7:** The sixth: When it had fully constructed the ordered spiritual sphere, it arose and sent forth a multitude of spiritual forces and many active divine truths, so that they would establish and guard the complete boundary of that ordered sphere on every side, until it had finished constructing all the works of regeneration. And at the completion [GAP-6] of all the works, it gathered some of these forces into its interior repositories of good and truth, and it stationed others in states of perpetual spiritual vigilance.

**¶8:** The seventh: At the time when the Divine Wisdom made manifest dis­played the form of its glory — the image of divine truth made visible — the Lord's operative power [GAP-7] set in place many governing goods and active truths. They [GAP-8: — the text here is lost, but the spiritual sense requires that these goods and truths acted in concert —] They took hold of that spiritual structure, so that the entire edifice of regeneration [GAP-9: — the sense requires: might stand firm and —] not [GAP-10: — the sense requires: collapse or turn against —] one another against [GAP-11] the wisdom which it had [GAP-12: — the sense requires: established and implanted throughout the whole].

**¶9:** Also another great and glorious act it will accomplish at the consummation: it is [GAP-13] the ultimate [GAP-14] completed form of the Divine Human — the final image of regeneration — which it will raise up into the eternal states of [GAP-15] wisdom. And it [GAP-16: — the sense requires: enters] in, and it takes hold, and it strikes down [GAP-17: — the sense requires: whatever remains of falsity and evil], and [GAP-18] it builds, and it [GAP-19: — the sense requires: perfects or completes], and it [GAP-20: — the sense requires: gathers all regenerated states into unity].

---

*Note on ¶9:* The "Last Statue" (GAP-14) is the most striking correspondence in the passage. A statue is an image fashioned to completion — the ultimate external form into which interior life is received. Spiritually, this is the fully realized Divine Human form within the regenerate person: the final work, raised into eternity. The sequence of verbs — entering, seizing, smiting, building — describes the Lord's final act of purification and glorification in one continuous motion.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: The Living Spirit has done seven [wo]rks with his strength.
[The fi]rst: He brought the First Man up from the contest, the way a pearl is [brought] up from the sea.
[The second: He spread about the one who had rebelled, he crucified][h]im in every body.
The third: He [tr]ampled, piled up, and pierced the essences of death.
[The f]ourth: He constructed the ships of light.

The fi[f]th: He evoked his five sons, and distributed them about. They [took] possession of the zone, they bore up under all the universe's weight. Also, he evoked three living words. He set [them] upon the th[re]e vessels, another one upon the giant. [Again, he evoked the] summons, that it might be mixed with the five shining men.

The sixth: When he had constructed the zone he aro[se] and s[e]nt forth a multitude of powers and many [angel]s; so that they would bound the circuit of the z[o]ne on every si[de], un[t]il he finished [co]nstructing the works. And at the end [of] all the [wor]ks he to[ok s]ome of them into his storehouses, and he appointed others at the watch-posts.

The [sev]enth: A[t the] time when the Ambass[ador dis]pl[aye]d his glorious imag[e], the L[iving] Spirit [established] many [go]ds and angels. They [ ... ] Th[ey to]ok hold of it, that the entire building [might stand and] not [ ... / ... ] one another against [the] light, which he had [set in them]

Also another gr[ea]t and glorious work he will enact at the e[nd] is [the] Last [Statue], which he will bring up to the aeons of [light]; and he [enters] in, and [he ta]kes hold, and he smites [the darkness], and [he] builds, and he [perfects], and he [gathers]hem.

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading says "drawn up" and the Kephalaia simile requires a pearl "brought up" from the sea; the editor's "brought" is the natural verb for this action and matches the correspondential sense of raising a precious interior truth from the abyss.

fills.original: The second: He spread about the one who had rebelled, he crucified
fills.explanation: The spiritual reading confirms "laid open the selfhood that had risen in rebellion, and fixed" — in Manichaean natural-plane vocabulary, "spread about the one who had rebelled" = laid open the rebellious selfhood, and "crucified" = fixed fast, which is the well-known Manichaean concept of the Jesus patibilis nailed into all matter.

The spiritual reading says "assumed governance of the ordered spiritual sphere" — "took possession of the zone" is the standard Kephalaia expression for the five sons assuming control, and "took" is the required verb.

The three living words are the antecedent; "He set them upon the three vessels" distributes each living word to its corresponding vessel, matching the spiritual reading's "each upon one of the three containing forms."

The spiritual reading says "It further called forth the divine invitation"; in the Kephalaia's register, "Again, he evoked the" introduces the summons — the divine calling — continuing the pattern of successive evocations in this paragraph.
The spiritual reading says "at the completion of all the works"; the preposition "of" is grammatically required to connect "at the end" with "all the works."
The spiritual reading says "set in place many governing goods and active truths"; "established" is the natural Kephalaia verb for the Living Spirit installing cosmic powers in their stations.

The spiritual reading says "might stand firm and not"; the building metaphor requires a verb of structural integrity — "that the entire building might stand and not [collapse]" is the natural completion.
The spiritual reading confirms "the wisdom" (= "the light" in the Kephalaia's natural register); the definite article "the" before "light" is grammatically required.

The spiritual reading says "established and implanted throughout the whole"; in the Kephalaia's register, "set in them" describes the light placed within the cosmic structures and powers, which the gods and angels must guard.
The spiritual reading says "it is the ultimate completed form"; the definite article "the" is grammatically required before "Last Statue."

The "Last Statue" (ⲁⲛⲇⲣⲓⲁⲥ) is a well-attested Manichaean eschatological concept — the completed form assembled from all rescued light; the spiritual reading confirms this as the fully realized Divine Human form raised into eternity.
The spiritual reading says "eternal states of wisdom"; in the Kephalaia, "aeons of light" is the standard designation for the realm of the Father of Greatness — light corresponding to divine wisdom.

The spiritual reading says "enters"; in the sequence of eschatological verbs (enters in, takes hold, smites, builds, perfects, gathers), "enters in" describes the Living Spirit's active entry into the final cosmic process.

The spiritual reading says "whatever remains of falsity and evil"; in the Manichaean natural register, "the darkness" is the encompassing term for all evil that the Living Spirit smites in the final eschatological action.
The subject throughout this sequence of parallel clauses is the Living Spirit; "he" is required to maintain the consistent pattern of "and he [verb]."

The spiritual reading says "perfects or completes"; in the eschatological verb sequence (enters, takes hold, smites, builds, perfects, gathers), "perfects" describes bringing the Last Statue to its completed form before the final gathering.

The spiritual reading says "gathers all regenerated states into unity"; "gathers" + the surviving "t]hem" yields "gathers them," describing the Living Spirit's final act of collecting all purified light into the Last Statue.
